_comment: Station facts: everything about YOUR receiver, rig and measured limits.
Edit this file. Keys starting with an underscore are notes and are ignored.
The values shipped here describe the station this program was built on:
a Nooelec NESDR SMArTee XTR (E4000) and a NESDR SMArt v5 (R820T) on Windows.
Run `marsad config` to see what is loaded and from where.
_rtl_sdr_dir: Folder holding rtl_power.exe etc., relative to this file. Searched before PATH.
_rtl_power_exe: Optional. Which rtl_power to run: a name ("rtl_power" picks the stock build on purpose) or a path relative to this file. Unset, marsad runs rtl_power_gainfix when it is installed (packaging/rtl_power_gainfix/BUILD.md: it keeps the R820T/R860 gain and does not overflow on strong carriers) and the stock rtl_power with a warning when it is not.
_location: Set once to record outdoor weather (Open-Meteo, no key) and the sun's elevation in every sidecar's auto_conditions, e.g. {"location": {"lat": 51.48, "lon": -0.01}} in decimal degrees, in station.local.json beside station.json (git ignores it, so the station's position stays off GitHub; it is laid over this file when marsad loads), west and south negative. Two decimals (~1 km) is plenty. Without it those parts record the reason instead.
_retune_ms_per_hop_fftw: rtl_power_fftw overhead, measured 2026-10-22 on this PC: 59 ms per hop (retune + first read) and 16 ms per extra 1.6 MB buffer read within a hop (91 ms at -t 1 and 2.4 MS/s). Built into marsad; set retune_ms_per_hop_fftw and read_ms_per_buffer_fftw here to override.
_retune_ms_per_hop: Time rtl_power loses retuning between hops. Measured 2026-10-13 on one USB stack; run `marsad calibrate-retune` to measure yours.

xtr.label: Nooelec NESDR SMArTee XTR (E4000, zero-IF)
xtr._gaps_mhz: E4000 PLL lock gap, measured on SN 08701076 with rtl_test -t. Re-measure per unit.

_receivers: device = USB index as rtl_test lists them. Not guaranteed across replugs; check rtl_test before a long run.
_spur_families_mhz: Harmonic families the analyser tags automatically. Order matters: tags are written in this order. Changing the list changes every peaks.csv, so do it between comparison sets, not inside one.
_readout_families_mhz: Families the live view names when you hover a line. 14.4 is the real RTL2832U fundamental (measured 2026-10-16).
_detection_floor_db: Smallest change compare-runs believes, by whether the hardware was touched between runs (measured 2026-10-17).

LS.note: PLL gap to rtl_power's 2147.48 MHz ceiling

wide.note: Overview (766 hops, 36 s retune floor); sweeps through the gap, analyser masks it

burst23.note: 1265.44 MHz burst hunt; 2 hops, ~95% listening, hop centres offset

top.note: 2147-2187 MHz, above rtl_power's 2^31 ceiling; 22 hops of 2.4 MHz, 18.75 kHz bins

h1.note: hydrogen line, one hop centred on 1420.4058 MHz, 1.17 kHz bins, 60 s per spectrum; --baseline FILE for an off-source spectrum

_presets: Named ranges for `marsad run <preset> <duration>`. Keep `custom` so a hand-built range is recorded as custom rather than masquerading as a preset.

baseline.note: chain baseline - one settings profile for terminated, cage A/B and every cascade step

gap-probe.note: the XTR's blind spot - v5 only, fingerprint of the retracted survey

_builder_profiles: Extra named profiles the scan builder offers; they emit `custom` to the CLI.

known_mhz.t: ADS-B transponders (use the v5; 1095 is the XTR's gap edge)
E4000 PLL lock gap, measured on this unit
broadband pedestal seen on the v5 2026-10-16, ~8 dB, steady; suspected front-end compression
604.2 kHz comb (NOT the 600 kHz family), r=0.885; internal vs external unresolved
ARSR radar: 12.000 s rotation, 113.8 us chirp, staggered PRF
28.8 MHz x51 - ours, strongest of the family
MSS uplink - 1633.47 found here at 39% occupancy, unexplained
AWS-3 uplink - strongest daytime signals, absent all night
strongest external line, ~100% occupancy, not ours

_known_mhz: What this station already knows is in the band. Shown by the scan builder for whatever range is selected. k = bad | spur | (plain).
_chain_modules: The physical rig, in signal order, for the scan builder. The source and the SDR are always present; the rest can be unchecked.
_recorder: marsad watch (RECORDER_DESIGN.md). pool: folder for captures, relative to this file or absolute; pool_gb and daily_gb are soft caps, nothing is ever deleted - when full, events are still catalogued and fingerprinted but no IQ is written. serials: which dongle is which role, matched by serial number, never by USB index. ppm: each radio's measured frequency error by serial (reported minus true, per million), 0 until measured. band_tiers: first matching row wins; anything not listed is open. A private band NEVER has its raw IQ written to disk - only a 20 ms x 1 kHz power spectrogram, flagged PRIVATE: do not decode (CLAUDE.md ground rule). reference_carriers_mhz: steady known carriers, captured once a day, and never treated as clock artefacts.

defaults.lna: Nooelec LaNA, bias-tee powered, at the antenna pigtail
defaults.filter: Nooelec Flamingo+ FM v2 notch (88-108 MHz)
defaults.chain_order: antenna > Flamingo+ FM notch > Nooelec LaNA > 8 ft coax > SMA bulkhead > SDR (caged) > USB extension > USB bulkhead > 16 ft USB > PC

_defaults: Last-used answers to the sidecar questions. `marsad run` rewrites this section after every run; everything else in this file is left alone.
